 IITF 2026: SEBI to issue AIML guidelines soon, steps up cyber defences amid rising threats
 Written By Tarun Sharma • Published: 9:00 AM, Nov 16, 2026 | Updated: 9:00 AM, Nov 16, 2026 SEBI is working on strengthening its AI capabilities through international initiatives and supervisory toolkits, said its Chairman TK Pandey. He also said SEBI is reviewing the regulatory framework to ensure that the use of AI by market participants does not compromise investor protection, market safety or integrity.
 With a continuous rise in cyber-attacks, especially following the Binance incident , SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday that it has been assured that its system is continuously evolving to protect against any new disruptions, and stated that guidelines for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) in the markets will be issued soon.
 “Vulnerability testing, patch testing, patching quickly, all these activities are continuously taking place,” Pandey told reporters on the sidelines of the 2026 India International Trade Fair in the national capital after inaugurating SEBI’s pavilion at the event.
 He also said that AI, cybersecurity and quantum were discussed in detail during the just-concluded board meeting of the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO).
 Talking about detailed guidelines for the responsible use of AI/ML, he said that the proposed guidelines would focus on establishing appropriate guardrails for AI use, including disclosures, accountability of regulated entities and a ‘human-in-the-loop’ approach to ensure that critical decisions are subject to human oversight.
 In June 2025, SEBI floated a consultation paper proposing guiding principles for responsible usage of AI/ML applications/models in securities markets. These guiding principles are intended to optimise benefits and minimise potential risks associated with the integration of AI/ML-based applications in securities markets to safeguard investor protection, market integrity and financial stability.
 Pandey said the regulator has been continuously strengthening its cybersecurity framework to address rising cyber threats. He highlighted growing concerns over cyberattacks targeting financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms, as well as digital frauds involving social media influencers.
 Following emerging threats, the regulator also introduced a structured incident response mechanism in May this year, aligned with the Financial Stability Board’s FIRE reporting template.
 On quantum computing-related risks, the Chairman said SEBI is undertaking an inventory of cryptographic systems and identifying areas where cryptography is being used to assess potential vulnerabilities. He said markets globally are preparing for the risks posed by quantum computing, with concerns expected to become more pronounced around 2032–35, and stressed the need to complete preparations well in advance.
 Speaking on AI adoption, he said SEBI has also developed several supervisory tools, including its ‘Sudarshan’ tool, which is being demonstrated at international regulatory forums.
 The regulator is also working on strengthening its AI capabilities through international initiatives and supervisory toolkits, he said, while adding that SEBI is reviewing the regulatory framework to ensure that the use of AI by market participants does not compromise investor protection, market safety or integrity.
 On startups and the listing framework, the SEBI chief also said the regulator has formed a working group to examine ways to make the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) more attractive for startups, particularly deep-tech and biotech companies that require long gestation periods before generating profits.
 He said the existing platform has not gained the desired traction, and the regulator is reviewing potential changes to help such companies access public markets at an earlier stage. The objective is to provide investors clarity about the higher risks associated with such businesses while allowing them to participate in their long-term growth potential.
 Organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 is being held from November 14 to 27.
 Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The event has brought together the country’s development, entrepreneurship and cultural heritage on one platform, featuring more than 3,500 exhibitors across 17 halls and over one lakh square metres of exhibition space.
 Participation includes 32 States and Union Territories, 51 Central Ministries, departments, PSUs and public sector banks, as well as 11 countries including Thailand, Iran, Ghana, Nepal, Afghanistan, the UAE, Turkey, China, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.
 The first five days, from November 14 to 18, are reserved for B2B visitors. The fair opens to the general public from November 19 to 27.
